correctness.rationale: For p in {5,7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31}, t^2 != 4 is exactly the squarefree genus-three condition. Cartier on regular differentials gives the three-by-three matrix with repeated A_p and central B_p; the superspecial criterion is precisely A_p=B_p=0. The exact multinomial formula, modular polynomial Euclidean gcds (1,t,t,1,1,t,t,1,t(t^2-20)), and an independent full coefficient expansion for all parameters in each F_p establish the claimed complete geometric root loci, not just numerical samples. Smoothness at 0,+/-12 in F31 follows from t^2!=4. No unproved extension beyond p31 is made.

value.rationale: The dihedral-symmetric genus-three family is a classical natural one-dimensional moduli locus. A parameter t=0 with extra symmetry was known; asking when its superspecial locus first has an off-center point is a natural stratum-boundary/cutoff question. The p31 gcd acquires t^2-20 unexpectedly while all earlier eligible primes have gcd 1 or t. This precise complete first-occurrence statement is reusable as an exact modular-family example and a genus-three superspecial enumeration test, and is not an arbitrary slice or an unmotivated count. It claims no general downstream theorem or geometric isomorphism census.
